item.title: Ebola scare in Adamawa: NCDC confirms negative tests
item.description: …Two suspected cases test negative after two rounds of laboratory tests By Chioma Obinna The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) last night said two suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases in Adamawa State tested negative after two rounds of laboratory tests, assuring Nigerians that the confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) remains the only confirmed infection reported in the country. The agency said the two individuals, who presented with symptoms suggestive of Ebola in Yola, were isolated as public health authorities commenced investigations and appropriate response measures. In a press statement yesterday, the Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, said the report was received by the Adamawa State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) in the early hours of October 30, 2026. He said samples collected from the individuals were subjected to laboratory testing to establish the cause of their illness, adding that both tested negative for Ebola after two rounds of testing. “Fortunately, the samples turned out negative for EBV after two rounds of testing,” Idris said. He clarified that there was currently no laboratory-confirmed Ebola case in Adamawa, stressing that the index case previously confirmed in the FCT remained the only confirmed case in Nigeria. “At this juncture, I wish to commend the efforts of the Adamawa State’s Commissioner for Health and his team for their proactive approach. NCDC will continue to provide appropriate technical support to the Adamawa State Government to strengthen their response operations,” he said. The latest development comes amid heightened public health vigilance following the confirmation of a Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja involving a traveller who arrived in Nigeria from Uganda. The emergence of the suspected cases in Adamawa had raised concerns about a possible spread of the disease, prompting the state and federal health authorities to activate investigation and precautionary measures. However, the negative laboratory results have ruled out Ebola infection in the two individuals, based on the tests reported by the NCDC. Idris urged Nigerians to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information or speculation about the situation. “We urge members of the public to remain calm and avoid sharing unverified information or speculation about the situation. The public is encouraged to obtain information from official government and public health communication channels,” he said. The NCDC director-general, however, emphasised the need for continued vigilance, noting that Ebola was a serious infectious disease requiring prompt identification, appropriate clinical management and effective infection prevention and control measures. item.title: Barca hammer Alaves 6-1 to retain Liga top spot
item.description: Raphinha and Lamine Yamal struck twice each as Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats. Earlier Atletico Madrid, second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved back two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou. Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend’s La Liga home Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick’s side found their groove once more. Raphinha netted twice in the first half, either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval. Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca’s sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves. There was a minute’s silence at the start of each of the day’s matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions. Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga’s top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form. Midfield maestro Pedri played in Lopez, who pulled the ball across for the Brazil international to bundle home. Alaves came close through Abde Rebbach before Lopez doubled Barcelona’s lead in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, Lopez smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it. Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca’s lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal. Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera. Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time. Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up. Yamal got Barca’s fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal. Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca’s sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on. – Seven in a row – Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone’s Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante. Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions. “I’m very happy with the team’s work,” Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar. “We’re very far from the end of the season… we’ll keep going game by game.” Alex Baena, the visito

item.title: Ortom hits back at ex-envoy Tarzoor, highlights governance achievements
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Former Benue State Governor, Chief Samuel Ortom, has challenged Ambassador Terhemen Tarzoor to account for his record in public office, accusing him of sustained attacks on his person over the defeat he suffered during the 2015 governorship election in the state. Recall that the former Nigerian envoy to Namibia had, during a recent media outing criticised the former governor over what he described as uncomplimentary remarks about Governor Hyacinth Alia and his administration. Ortom described Tarzoor’s criticism as “a manifestation of the bitterness he has harboured since his defeat in the 2015 governorship election,” alleging that the former governorship candidate had consistently used media engagements to attack him more than a decade after the election. He said Tarzoor’s latest comments, ostensibly in defence of Governor Hyacinth Alia, were an attempt to remain politically relevant. He added that the ambassador had misrepresented his remarks by claiming that he described the actions of the people of Benue as “shenanigans.” “Chief Ortom could never have used such a term to disparage the people of Benue State. If anything, his reference was to the antics of individuals like Tarzoor, whose utterances and conduct appear calculated to sow discord, deepen divisions and breed acrimony in the polity,” he said. Ina statement.by his media Aide, Paul Zege, the former governor questioned Tarzoor’s record as Speaker of the Benue State House of Assembly, asking him to identify the developmental projects he attracted to his constituency and the achievements he could point to as evidence of his contributions to the people. He also raised questions about the controversial creation of a Fulani ward in Makurdi Local Government Area, LGA, which he said was subsequently reversed after the exercise was reportedly found to be fraudulent. Ortom further questioned Tarzoor’s record as Nigeria’s ambassador to Namibia, alleging that his tenure failed to establish a notable diplomatic legacy, urging the former Speaker to focus on issues affecting the state rather than engage in what he described as persistent attacks on him. Defending his administration’s record, Ortom said security was one of the defining issues of his tenure, particularly his opposition to open grazing and the repeated attacks on farming communities. He said his administration “enacted the Open Grazing Prohibition and Ranches Establishment Law of 2017, established the Benue State Livestock Guards, supported the Community Volunteer Guards and provided logistics to security agencies. “He could have chosen the politically convenient path. He could have remained silent, avoided confrontation with powerful interests and maintained cordial relations with the Federal Government of the day. Instead, he chose to stand with his people and defend their lands when he believed the survival of his people was at stake,” he said. item.title: 2027: Don’t be deceived, vote for Tinubu, South-East govs tell Igbos
item.description: Governors of Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo States have urged the people not to be deceived by political distractions but to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. The governors made the call on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East, held at Okpara Square, Enugu. The governors are Prof. Charles Soludo of Anambra, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi, Dr Peter Mbah of Enugu and Sen. Hope Uzodimma of Imo. Speaking, Mbah urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms. He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the Federal Government’s economic reforms. The governor urged women to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the Jan. 16, 2027, and subsequent elections. “A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges. We must finish the journey we all started together,” he said. Mbah described South Easterners as strategic people who had established businesses and relationships beyond the zone, urging them to participate actively in the political process. Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-East, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women in Enugu within 48 hours. He said the beneficiaries received cash support, assistance with hospital bills and tools to enable them to generate income. According to him, the programme is designed to make women wealth creators rather than perpetual beneficiaries of financial assistance. “When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said. He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the empowerment tools and extend the benefits to their families and communities. Also speaking, Uzodimma described the rally as historic and commended the First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, for empowering women across the South-East. He reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu. He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructural and economic development in the South-East. “We are now seeing good roads, electricity, and health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said. The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the federal government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development. “We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said. item.title: Kane Misses Penalty After Ballon d’Or Feat As Bayern Held By Dortmund
item.description: Fabio Silva’s 89th-minute goal earned Borussia Dortmund a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich after Harry Kane missed a penalty in a see-saw Bundesliga clash on Saturday. Bayern were 1-0 up when Kane, playing his first match since winning the Ballon d’Or on Monday, rattled his second-half spot kick against the crossbar. Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy levelled shortly after, but Kane helped Bayern retake the lead when he set up a Dayot Upamecano goal. In the final minute, substitutes Konstantinos Karetsas and Silva combined to grab Dortmund a share of the spoils. “Coming back twice here in Munich is no easy feat. We earned a well-deserved point here today,” Dortmund coach Niko Kovac told Sky Germany, adding his side “never stopped believing in ourselves.” Dortmund’s Guinean forward #09 Serhou Guirassy (C) scores the 1-1 goal during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) The result leaves the two sides level atop the Bundesliga table, with defending champions Bayern ahead on goal difference. It is just the fourth time in the past 18 ‘Klassiker’ matches that Bayern have not emerged victorious. In addition to the late draw, Bayern, who are without Vincent Kompany as he recovers from a virus, will be concerned by further injuries to their undermanned forward line ahead of Tuesday’s trip to Atletico Madrid. Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all subbed out on Saturday, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz already out with injury. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the draw appeared “costly”, with Saibari and Gnabry’s injuries “somewhat serious”. Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich, who returned after missing three matches after the sudden death of his father, said: “It’s been a really, really hard week, but you can forget during the game. “Other than the result today, you have to say we’re going through difficult moments right now, now with the injuries we picked up.” Kane was honoured pre-match with his Ballon d’Or shown to the Bayern faithful for the first time. Bayern Munich’s English forward Harry Kane shows his Ballon d’Or trophy to the fans prior to the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. item.title: Clashes Erupt In France As Thousands Protest Cost Of Living, Inequality
item.description: A police officer in Paris was injured after being struck by a Molotov cocktail as clashes erupted in the capital and other cities during protests across France against soaring living costs and inequality. Hundreds of thousands of people, some dressed for Halloween, demonstrated across France in a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful demonstrations. But the Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez pointed to an “extraordinary” level of violence from some, blaming far-left extremist groups for attacks on security forces. He described the throwing of a Molotov cocktail at a riot police officer in Paris as an “attempted murder,” adding that the officer had escaped with minor injuries. “We are fully prepared for those looking for confrontation tonight,” he added. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police, AFP journalists saw. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. ‘Engulfed In Flames’ Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said those responsible for the Molotov attack must be “punished with the utmost severity.” “The images of a police officer engulfed in flames after being targeted with incendiary devices are unbearable,” Le Pen said on X. A French riot gendarme mobile has flames rising up his uniform after being hit by a Molotov cocktail during a charge against demonstrators at the end of a demonstration part of a nationwide day of protests over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students organisations, in Paris on October 31, 2026. Photo by SAMEER AL-DOUMY / AFP A night-time curfew was to be imposed in the central Paris Republique and Chatelet-Les Halles neighbourhoods from 11:00 pm to 6:00 am on Saturday and Sunday. Police arrested more than 420 people across the country. The interior ministry said that “radical elements” in cities including Bordeaux, Toulouse and Marseille had attempted to enter city centres “with the aim of carrying out vandalism and looting”. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people. ‘Attack On Freedom’ Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, marched through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. item.title: German Police, Protesters Clash After ‘Gen Z’ Protest, Several Police Officers Injured
item.description: German police and protesters clashed across the country Saturday following massive youth-led protests, with authorities using water cannon and pepper spray as masked demonstrators hurled fireworks, stones and bottles. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined protests nationwide that were organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse. Police were pelted with projectiles in the western city of Frankfurt, and responded by using water cannon and pepper spray as they sought to clear protesters. “Incidents of stones and fireworks being thrown at the emergency services continue to occur,” police said on X. “We are taking action against these troublemakers.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. ‘Boiling Point’ In Berlin, a protest that was not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. Police in the eastern city of Leipzig also used pepper spray after protests turned violent while a police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have made several arrests. Police detain a protester after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere, with some dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween.They waved signs that read “Time for resistance”, and “Merz must go”, in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz. “I think it’s really important to show solidarity with all the other protests currently happening across Europe, including in France,” Milla, a 20-year-old student who only gave her first name, told AFP in Berlin. “I’ve been waiting for a long time for something to finally really happen, and for people to tackle this with a bit more force. I believe that today here is the first step.” Marius, a 23-year-old care worker, added that “politicians need to know about this… the situation is slowly reaching boiling point.” “I think we can all feel that this just isn’t working anymore,” he added. The movement’s complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation. item.title: Binance says has covered 90% of $6.3 billion hack losses
item.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Saturday it has used company money to buy tokens to replenish 90 percent of $6.3 billion stolen in a huge hacking attack. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said on X. Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes, said the remaining 10 percent of tokens are “less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts.” The company said it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack. Binance said Friday it was working to resolve what it called a “complex attack” with several “points of breach.” Investigators pointed to hackers linked to North Korea as being responsible. The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on news of the cyberattack. Binance suspended user withdrawals after the incident, but said in its latest update they were on track to resume Sunday. The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. President Donald Trump said Friday the United States was looking into the hack, and the FBI said it was “engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity” and was ready to investigate. item.title: Insecurity didn’t begin in Tinubu’s administration – Dogara
item.description: A former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Mr Yakubu Dogara, says Nigeria’s security challenges predate the administration of President Bola Tinubu. Dogara, who is the Chancellor of Achievers University, Owo, Ondo State, made the assertion at the institution’s 16th convocation ceremony, where 836 graduands received various academic qualifications. He said terrorism, insurgency, banditry, kidnapping and communal violence had been entrenched in the country long before the current administration assumed office in May 2023. According to him, the nation’s security problems are rooted in years of porous borders, illegal arms proliferation, high youth unemployment and the spread of extremist ideologies. “Insecurity in Nigeria did not begin with this administration. This is no excuse, because the facts need no defence. Terrorism, insurgency, banditry, kidnapping and communal violence did not arrive in 2023,” Dogara said. He explained that the security situation developed over several years, stressing that its roots went deep long before the current government took over. Dogara, however, noted that President Tinubu had consistently identified national security as a top priority and major responsibility of his administration. The chancellor charged the graduands to deploy their talents, creativity and innovation toward national development. Speaking, the Pro-Chancellor of the university, Prof. Bode Ayorinde, acknowledged the progress made in expanding access to tertiary education, but expressed concern over the job prospects of graduates. Ayorinde cited figures from the National Universities Commission (NUC), which put the number of universities in Nigeria at 312 as of June 2026, comprising 77 federal, 67 state-owned, and 168 private institutions. He said although the growth represented a huge investment in human capital by parents, governments and lecturers, deliberate efforts must be made to create viable opportunities for graduates after school. In her address, the Vice-Chancellor of the institution, Prof. Omolola Irinoye, reiterated the university’s commitment to providing quality education that combines intellectual growth, practical skills, character building and social responsibility. Irinoye said that there were 98 First Class graduates in the academic session, attributing the performance to the institution’s investment in quality assurance, staff development and a conducive learning environment. According to her, the university also operates flexible payment arrangements to accommodate students from different socioeconomic backgrounds. “The institution’s scholarship programme was designed to ensure that financial constraints did not prevent deserving students from acquiring university education. “The university has 100 per cent tuition scholarship in 17 academic programmes, with 80 per cent tuition scholarship in five academic programmes while there were also 70 per cent tuition scholarship in other five academic programmes,” she said. item.title: Katsina Debunks Campaign Violence Claims, Orders Probe Into Yankara Incident
item.description: The Katsina State Government has dismissed reports linking the incident that occurred in Yankara, Faskari Local Government Area, to Governor Dikko Radda’s Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign, describing such claims as false and misleading. In a statement, the government said preliminary findings showed that the disturbance stemmed from a disagreement between participants in a Maulud procession and security personnel over designated procession routes, resulting in confusion along a public street in Yankara. It stressed that the incident was entirely unrelated to thegovernor’s campaign activities or the Tinubu-Dikko campaign rally held in Faskari. According to the government, Governor Radda passed through Yankara without incident on his way to Faskari, where he paid a courtesy visit to the District Head’s Palace and was received by the district head and other traditional rulers. The governor, it said, later proceeded to the Faskari Local Government secretariat, where he inspected ongoing renovation works at the secretariat and council chambers before attending the campaign rally and interacting with residents and supporters. Governor Dikko Radda addresses a crowd of supporters at the Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign in Faskari Local Government Area of Katsina State on October 31, 2026. The state government urged relevant security agencies to carry out a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that those responsible are identified where necessary. In the statement signed by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ibrahim Mohammed, the government appealed to residents to remain calm, uphold peace, and avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing unnecessary tension. Violence was reported in Yankara town on Saturday after suspected hoodlums attacked supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), leaving several people injured and a campaign vehicle set ablaze. Eyewitnesses said the attackers allegedly ambushed APC supporters heading to Governor Radda’s campaign rally in Faskari, disrupting movement along the major road and causing panic among residents. Angry youths were also alleged to have blocked the route the campaign convoy was expected to use. item.title: FG deploys experts to Ogun over recurring gas emissions in schools
item.description: By James Ogunnaike The Federal Government has deployed a specialised technical team to Ogun State to investigate recurring subsurface gas emissions that have triggered health concerns and disrupted academic activities in secondary schools across the Ijebu axis. The intervention, coordinated by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), is aimed at establishing the geological source of the emissions and recommending lasting solutions to the recurring incidents affecting schools and surrounding communities. The deployment followed reports of localised gas seepages suspected to have caused oxygen depletion and breathing difficulties among students and other residents in the affected communities. Speaking during a joint press briefing and commencement of a site assessment in Ijebu Ode on Saturday, the Federal Government’s Ad-hoc Committee said preliminary indications suggested that the emissions could be associated with natural subsurface geological processes rather than leaks from petroleum pipelines. The team, however, stressed the need for further technical investigations to establish the actual source and nature of the emissions. Speaking at the briefing, the team leader and Assistant Director at the NUPRC, Prosper Okonedo, said the Commission had constituted the committee following an initial assessment conducted by the Ogun State Government. Okonedo explained that the Commission’s Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyawa Eyesan, directed the deployment of experts from its Lagos regional office to collaborate with the state government and investigate the situation. According to him, “about two weeks ago, the Commission Chief Executive of NUPRC, Mrs. Oritsemeyawa Eyesan, advised that we set up an ad-hoc committee from the Lagos regional office to come to the state because the state government had conducted an initial assessment and submitted their report.” He disclosed that the Commission had also been investigating similar incidents in other parts of the country, including communities in Rivers and Delta states. “Presently, we have a study group known as the Epe Study Group. They are looking into similar issues in a village community in Rivers State, and there is one right now in Delta State where we have established that gas seepage is emanating from the subsurface. “However, for this state, we cannot really say what it is right now. That is why we are here, and we are going to deploy to the site to see the situation for ourselves, even though the state government had reported seepages of gas affecting certain secondary schools in some communities,” he said. Okonedo said the federal government was committed to working with the Ogun State government to address the situation and safeguard residents. “The government is there to ensure the welfare and well-being of the Nigerian people. item.title: Troops neutralize suspected bandits in Kogi shootout
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Sector 3, Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke have neutralized a suspected bandit following an intelligence-led ambush along the Adankolo–Apata Road in Kogi State. The operation, conducted on Saturday 31 October 2026, followed credible intelligence on the movement of suspected terrorists around communities in Kabba-Bunu and Lokoja Local Government Areas of the state. Spokesman of the Sector, Captain Ahmad Zubairu who made this known, said the troops acting on the intelligence, troops laid ambush at suspected bandits’ supply route. “The troops subsequently made contact with the suspected criminals who were subdued and forced to flee. “At about 9pm on the same day during exploitation, troops received information regarding the discovery of suspected bandits’ bodies towards Adankolo Forest. “On arrival at the location, troops found corpses of the two suspected bandits and recovered one locally made pistol, one cartridge and one empty case of 7.62mm special ammunition. “The Force Commander, Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke and General Officer Commanding 5 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General Moses Gara, commended the troops for their gallantry and successful execution of the operation. “He urged members of the public to continue supporting security agencies by providing timely and credible information on suspicious activities, stressing that security remains everybody’s responsibility. “The Force Commander reiterated the commitment of Operation Whirl Stroke to sustaining intelligence-led operations aimed at protecting lives and property across its Area of Responsibility.” The post Troops neutralize suspected bandits in Kogi shootout appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Iran says US tone has ‘changed’ as Washington seeks negotiations
item.description: Iran on Saturday said the tone of the United States had “completely changed” as Washington seeks to restart negotiations with the Islamic republic. While the US and Israel have upped their threats to order fresh strikes, Vice President JD Vance also sent a letter to Iranian officials in recent days in a bid to revive talks. “I read the letter. I haven’t yet responded. Their tone has completely changed,” Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran’s supreme national security council, said in a video broadcast on Iranian television. He said the change in tone was “a good sign” and showed Iran had “consolidated its victory”. Rezaei said he had not responded to the letter and would not comment further on its contents. His comments came as indirect mediation via Qatar continued, though Iranian officials said earlier on Saturday that they had no plans to meet with US officials. item.title: 2027: Miyetti Allah backs Tinubu’s re-election, cites livestock ministry
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The National President of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Baba Othman Ngelzarma, has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, citing the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development as a major step towards addressing decades of neglect of the livestock sector. Ngelzarma said pastoralists, cattle breeders and other livestock stakeholders across the country were prepared to support Tinubu for a second term in appreciation of his administration’s recognition of the economic importance of the sector. He spoke at a rally organised in Kaduna by the Fulbe APC Forum and Tinubu Yeso-Yeso Political Forum (TYPF), in collaboration with the Coalition of Pastoralists and Traders Associations and the Amalgamated Union of Livestock Dealers, Butchers and other stakeholders. The rally, held under the theme, “United for Inclusion, Representation and Prosperity,” attracted Fulani organisations, pastoralists, cattle breeders, livestock dealers, butchers, processors and political stakeholders from different parts of the country. Ngelzarma said the creation of the livestock ministry in July 2024 had fulfilled a longstanding demand by pastoralists and livestock operators, who had campaigned for a dedicated government institution to address challenges in the industry for several decades. “We are here today to extend our appreciation and support to the administration of President Tinubu. “The creation of the livestock ministry is something we have been advocating for and looking forward to for decades,” he said. He noted that the initiative had also encouraged some state governments to establish similar institutions to coordinate livestock development, describing it as an opportunity to address longstanding challenges confronting pastoralists and other operators in the industry. The Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Mukhtar Maiha, urged pastoralists, livestock farmers and other stakeholders to take advantage of the ministry’s programmes to improve productivity, expand their businesses and enhance their livelihoods. Maiha identified inadequate veterinary services, limited access to pasture and water, high feed costs, poor market infrastructure and low productivity as some of the factors that had hindered the growth of Nigeria’s livestock industry over the years. He said Nigeria had an estimated 58 million cattle, 124 million goats, 70 million sheep, 9.3 million pigs, 3.2 million donkeys, 700,000 camels and 300 million birds, describing the figures as enormous economic opportunities that could be harnessed through deliberate investments and improved management. The minister disclosed that seven veterinary hospitals had been completed and equipped under a World Bank-supported programme, while additional facilities were at various stages of completion. item.title: Gov. Lawal presents staff of office, vehicles to 19 Zamfara emirs
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal has presented staff of office and official vehicles to 19 emirs in Zamfara State. The coronation and presentation ceremony took place at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital. Dignitaries in attendance included His Eminence the Sultan of Sokoto, the Etsu Nupe, and the Emir of Gwandu. After their oaths of office, Governor Lawal presented staff of office to 11 first-class emirs and eight second-class emirs. Each newly coronated emir also received a GAC Ultra SUV (2025/2026 model), a Mikano ZNA Hilux vehicle and an EV Antique Model car (DDP). The vehicles are intended to support their travels and help them engage more closely with their communities. In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the ceremony reflected his administration’s recognition of the traditional institution as an enduring part of society and an important partner in promoting peace, stability and development. He noted that the ceremony also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to giving traditional rulers the recognition and institutional support they need to carry out their responsibilities effectively. He said, “The staff of office being presented today signifies the authority entrusted to you by the State. “It also represents a responsibility to govern your respective domains with fairness, wisdom, integrity, and compassion. “I expect every emir to carry out their responsibilities without discrimination, uphold justice, and ensure that the traditional institution remains accessible to all members of the community. “Our people must find guidance, fairness, and reassurance in their traditional rulers. “Recognising the importance of royal palaces as centres of traditional authority and community engagement, I reaffirm our commitment to completing the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the remaining royal palaces. “This is part of our broader effort to strengthen these institutions and improve the conditions in which traditional rulers carry out their responsibilities. “We are also providing official vehicles to the 19 emirs. These include GAC ULTRA SUVs (2025/2026 models), MIKANO ZNA HILUX vehicles, and EV ANTIQUE MODEL cars (DDP). “This provision is intended to facilitate travel across your respective emirates, encourage closer engagement with your communities, and improve coordination with government institutions. “I expect these vehicles to be properly maintained and used responsibly in support of your official duties.” The governor also urged the royal fathers to build a productive partnership between their emirates and the state government. Earlier, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar, urged the newly coronated emirs to remain fully loyal to the authority. He also encouraged them to respect and uphold the dignity of the traditional institution as they discharge their duties. The post Gov. Lawal presents staff of office, vehicles to 19 Zamfara emirs appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sowore reacts as Ekiti police arrest 11 over attack
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested 11 suspects over the attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, Omoyele Sowore, and members of his team at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, the state capital. In a statement on Saturday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abutu Sunday, said operatives of the Rapid Response Squad arrested the suspects at their hideouts in the Atikankan area of the town at about 10pm on Friday, following a tip-off. It partly reads, “The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested eleven (11) suspects in connection with the alleged attack on Mr Omoyele Sowore, an African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, and other persons at Tawakalitu Restaurant, Dalimore Area of Ado-Ekiti. “The suspects are Joseph Tayo ’32yrs’, Olatunji Abayomi ’41yrs’, Isaac Amba ’22yrs’, Kehinde Ajigbana ’18yrs’, Tosin David ’18yrs’, Solomon Iyanu ’18yrs’, Ogunsola Ayomide ’21yrs’, Ojo Ayodeji ’22yrs’, Kayode Dada ’32yrs’, Segun Olatunji ’28yrs’ and Salami Emmanuel ’53yrs’. “Items recovered include two walkie-talkies, substances suspected to be Indian hemp and Colorado, two Indian hemp crushers, one pack of Rizla, seven ATM cards, thirteen mobile phones, two vehicle keys, one flash drive, one 5G MTN Wi-Fi device, identity cards, eight international passports, three complimentary cards, two suspected criminal charms, one gas lighter and ₦250.” The police said investigations were ongoing to establish the individual roles of the suspects and determine their possible connections with the attack. The Commissioner of Police, Falade Michael, assured residents that everyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The statement quoted him as saying that the command “will leave no stone unturned in ensuring that all those found culpable are brought to justice.” Reacting to the arrests, Sowore demanded that the alleged masterminds and sponsors of the attack be identified and brought to justice, insisting that the incident was a coordinated assault and not an ordinary altercation. The presidential candidate made the demand in a post on X on Saturday, describing the arrests as an admission that the incident was a violent attack. He also alleged that some of the attackers were associated with the City Boys group and called for investigations into possible links between the incident and officials of the state government. Sowore urged the Commissioner of Police, Falade Adegoroye Michael, and the Department of State Services to preserve and release CCTV footage from the scene to help identify those involved. “Arresting 11 suspects is not enough if those who planned, financed, coordinated and facilitated the attack remain untouched,” he wrote. He also demanded an explanation from the police over their initial description of the incident as an altercation. item.title: 2027: ‘Don’t be deceived, vote for Tinubu’ – South-East govs tell Igbo
item.description: Governors of Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo States have urged the people not to be deceived by political distractions but to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. The governors made the call on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East, held at Okpara Square, Enugu. Speaking, Mbah urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms. He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the Federal Government’s economic reforms. The governor urged women to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the Jan. 16, 2027, and subsequent elections. “A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges. We must finish the journey we all started together,” he said. Mbah described South Easterners as strategic people who had established businesses and relationships beyond the zone, urging them to participate actively in the political process. Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-East, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women in Enugu within 48 hours. He said the beneficiaries received cash support, assistance with hospital bills and tools to enable them to generate income. According to him, the programme is designed to make women wealth creators rather than perpetual beneficiaries of financial assistance. “When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said. He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the empowerment tools and extend the benefits to their families and communities. Uzodimma Also speaking, Uzodimma described the rally as historic and commended the First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, for empowering women across the South-East. He reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu. He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructural and economic development in the South-East. “We are now seeing good roads, electricity, health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said. The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the Federal Government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development. “We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said. item.title: Police repel bandits’ attack on Kebbi community
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has said that it is aware of the security incident in Ribah, Zuru Local Government Area, on 30th October 2026, when suspected bandits launched two successive attacks on the community. Police image maker, in a statement on Saturday, revealed that the first incident occurred at about 7:25 pm, when the assailants attempted to block Rambo Junction along the Ribah–Dirin Daji Road under Zuru emirate, as their attempt was promptly foiled by the joint security forces comprising the police, military and local vigilante group, who engaged them in a gun duel and dispersed them. The statement added that the attackers later regrouped and returned, shooting sporadically from different directions within the town. However, during the ensuing exchange, one Hassan Boder, aged 47, a security guard at a newly constructed filling station along Ribah–Kanya Road, was fatally hit by a bullet. Upon receipt of a distress call, the joint security team swiftly mobilised, engaged the attackers and successfully repelled them. Usman explained that security operations have since been intensified, with aggressive patrols ongoing to dominate the area and efforts underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Yes, we are aware of the attack and we have repelled it by forcing the terrorists to retreat due to superior firepower. The combined security forces have dominated the area to prevent further attacks on the communities,” he said. item.title: Clashes break out as hundreds of thousands protest in France
item.description: Police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in Paris and elsewhere on Saturday as hundreds of thousands marched across France against soaring living costs and police violence, with some demonstrators dressed as clowns and witches for Halloween. While the third consecutive weekend of nationwide protests was largely peaceful, tensions erupted in several cities later Saturday. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police. At least one incendiary device was also thrown at security forces. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. “A hard core of several hundred rioters” at the rear of the march attacked police with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail, the police prefecture said. Officers were seeking “to restore public order”, it added. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas, according to a journalist at the scene. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people, mostly young demonstrators. – ‘Dressed up as angry citizen’ – Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, walked through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. Placards read: “No need for tear gas to make our future look bleak” and “Dressed up as an angry citizen for Halloween.” A protester wearing a Marie-Antoinette costume (L) holds a placard reading “Give them brioche” flanked by a protester dressed as a wizard holding a placard reading “A potion for the revolution” during a demonstration in Lyon, central-eastern France on October 31, 2026, part of nationwide demonstrations over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students. “Exceptional” security deployment with 70,000 police officers and gendarmes mobilized and an alarmist tone: for Act III of the protests against the high cost of living, right in the middle of Halloween festivities, the authorities fear a repeat of the October 17 nightmare. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality. (Photo by JEFF PACHOUD / AFP) “We say no to the cost of living, no to the far right, yes to high school students’ demands, yes to giving citizens a voice,” said Camille Guerin, 31, a demonstrator in the western city of Nantes. Authorities said that some 320,000 people rallied across France including 70,000 in Paris. According to youth organisations, nearly half a million people demonstrated across the country, including 200,000 in Paris. item.title: US yet to decide on new Iran strikes, says Rubio
item.description: US President Donald Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran amid stalled peace talks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday. “We can achieve military objectives if we seek to,” Rubio told a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he was hosting G20 foreign ministers for a two-day meeting. But Rubio added that Trump “hasn’t made a decision” on further military action, amid reports that the US leader could attack after key midterm elections on Tuesday. “I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly,” Rubio said. While he slammed Tehran for “actively and openly” targeting commercial vessels for attack, Rubio also expressed Trump’s preference for a diplomatic solution to end war with Iran. But he did not commit to a timeline for talks. “I’m not going to characterize neither the progress on those talks nor any timeframe on it, other than to tell you that if there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it,” Rubio said. Iran’s supreme leader on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks, following threats to resume strikes after crucial elections. Trump earlier warned of the potential for fresh military action after US midterms, saying previously that he was weighing up whether to “finish them off.” But any further attack would spark concern among US allies. On Thursday, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told AFP: “We are calling for a diplomatic solution, and really, escalation does not benefit anyone.” AFP The post US yet to decide on new Iran strikes, says Rubio appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Africa’s First Ever Youth Olympics Open In Senegal
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, opened Saturday in the Senegalese capital, marking an historic moment for the continent. Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are omnipresent across Dakar, which is hosting nearly 2,700 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world. The event will see the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the young athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events. “Today it’s not just a nation that is welcoming the Youth Olympic Games; it’s an entire continent that is opening its arms”, Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye told a sport and development summit Saturday ahead of the Games’ opening ceremony. Senegal’s Influencer and TikToker Khaby Lame carries the Youth Olympic Flame on the eve of the opening ceremony of the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar on October 30, 2026. Photo by PATRICK MEINHARDT / AFP The Games will not only celebrate champions but also “our collective capacity to transform sport into an economic and social engine”, he said, emphasising that 130 years of Olympic history had passed before the Olympic flame ever landed on African soil. Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations. Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly, located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events. The Games are “showing the world our capacity (as Africa), a capacity that sometimes is underestimated”, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Saturday during the summit. According to Coventry, the opening ceremony will be televised live in more than 30 countries, with every African nation having committed to showing the Games live, she said. Sports Culture An opening ceremony Saturday evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games. A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event. The West African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene. Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or on weekends on the beach or in village squares. And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar’s iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise. While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics has struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal. Mexican athletes arrive with their suitcases at the Youth Olympic Village in Diamniadio, on October 29, 2026. (Photo by PATRICK MEINHARDT / AFP) Many are more concerned with the high cost of living, unemployment and economic hardship. “Once the Youth Olympic Games in Senega
